description.purpose: One screen, reached at /<mount>/ on the colony's one listener, that many agents and applications write onto at once. A view is a named, owned, optionally expiring piece of that screen: whoever sends one owns it, replaces it under the same name, and takes it down again. A store holds what is up, a code cell keeps that set and the display's object tree in agreement, and a display cell serves the page. Since 1.0.2 a `key` collision inside a component tree is a named refusal on `receipt` rather than a node that quietly disappears, and a key that is a plain number is refused with it. Since 1.1.0 the screen has two columns: `main`, wide, and `aside`, narrow, for the widgets that stand there whether or not anybody is talking -- and the order inside a column is the `ord` a view declared, then first appearance, never the last write. Since 2.0.0 the screen has no port of its own: the `web` cell it holds hangs on the colony's one listener under `override_params.web.mount` (`display` as shipped), so one reverse-proxy rule in front of that listener covers the whole colony. Since 1.2.0 the screen carries a microphone: a hold-to-talk button that joins a `voice:<call>` topic on the page's own socket, so the person looking at the screen can speak to the colony and hear it, provided a `voice` cell is mounted under the name the display was given (`voice_mount`, default `voice`). Since 2.0.1 that button says what it is doing while the browser asks for the microphone, tells a person to press again when the answer came after they let go, and treats a closed call as the end of a call rather than the end of the button: the next press joins again, and only a refused join is final. Since 2.1.0 the screen brings its own design language: the sheet and a catalogue of twenty-six components -- four windows and twenty-two pieces of content -- travel inside the `display-shell` definition, so an application names `display-pane` or `display-clock` in its tree and defines only what is its own. A screen recognises its own outdated vocabulary: the root carries a fingerprint of the definitions, and a running screen whose root holds another one gets the whole list defined again on its next pass, once. The faces are an operator asset with an empty default: `params.font_base` names the directory the two font files are served from, empty means no `@font-face` and the fallback stacks carry the type, and no font file ships in this repository. Since 2.2.0 the screen curates what it shows: every window carries a context and a relevance as hints, the root carries a focus number and per-context weights, the compose cell scores each window, hides what falls below the bar, gives exactly one window in `main` the focus rung, lets a window leave over two frames, and a title's presence follows the rung. A `timer` cell strikes at the moment the compose cell predicts, an `llm` cell may re-judge the whole screen on a content change, and a classified notice arrives on `in_notice`. Since 2.2.1 a hold survives the button moving under the pointer: the press captures the pointer, the state line has a height before it speaks, and a page that loses focus or goes hidden releases. Since 2.2.2 an application says `touched` (an epoch, as text) on a window whose content is new -- the screen compares a window's own props, and an answer in a child component is invisible to that comparison unless the application says so -- and the hold-to-talk button is a fixed point on the screen with its two lines floating above it. Since 2.2.3 a pass that computes the moment already ordered from the clock orders the same second again without removing it first, and the clock treats a repeated order as one order -- before, the re-add collided with the row the remove had just marked, and the moment never struck. Since 2.3.0 the screen answers three questions in three places: the canvas shows what is in focus, a dock at the right edge shows everything that is present -- one tile of one size per window, ordered by relevance, dual with the window it stands for -- and an OS mark at the bottom right is where a person speaks, the button the microphone capsule used to be. Presence and focus are two axes now: a judgement decides what is LARGE and never what exists, so the clock does not leave when the weather is asked about. `aside` is still accepted and is drawn as canvas. A window may say `topic`, so a standing window on the same subject takes a fresh answer instead of standing beside it, and `modal`, which is the only thing that may blur the canvas. The renderer knows its display: a `screens` setting gives each output a type, a viewing distance and its inputs, and one scale at the root carries the type and the furniture. A hook on the root runs the seconds of a countdown, plays a two-tone chime when a window arrives urgent, and moves a window into its tile and back. Since 2.3.2 the OS mark reads as »OS«: the ring opens to the right and the S sits on its rim, its outer edge on the ring's outer edge. Since 2.4.0 the screen has four levels and two ladders: an application declares which ladder a window competes on (`layer`, `canvas` or `modal`), the curator gives each ladder its own focus, and a window is drawn on the level its rung and its exit's slots put it on -- the loudest urgent in front, one active modal over the canvas, the canvas focus and as many `relevant` windows beside it as that screen carries. A tap on a tile is a touch on its window, everywhere at once and without asking the judge; a second tap puts it back in its tile; holding the OS mark touches the chat. A window may say how long it lingers after a touch, and where it sits in the dock -- the clock at the bottom, the weather above it, and an empty seat stays empty. Each exit carries its own dials (`dock_max`, `dock_default`) and shows as much of the one state as it can. The judge no longer sees any geometry. And a window may hold one line a person types into (`display-input`), which reaches the application as an event like a button does. Since 2.5.0 the screen is built to its description: one state per member in the store, the pass of the reference model step for step, the finger above the score (`led_until`), the chat closed by the `turn_id` of the answer's window, a dock cut per exit that never takes a window, the events `tap` and `hold`, and a switch at the mount root. Since 2.5.1 the curator runs one message at a time: `params.max_concurrency` is 1 on the compose cell, so the passes that read and write the one state row are handled in the order their events arrived instead of four of them at once. Since 2.6.0 a browser is only ever told what the store agreed to: the patch of a pass rides its own state write and is sent from the reply, so a write the compare-and-set refuses draws nothing at all and runs its pass again instead. It costs one message round trip per event and buys a screen that never draws a state it has to take back. Since 2.7.0 the curator keeps its state in memory and that round trip is gone: the compose cell runs `resident`, the store holds the applications' rows and one small rest row that is written only when it changes, one pass sends one patch, and a restart rebuilds the same screen out of the rows and the tree the display holds.
description.use_when: A person should be able to look at what several agents and applications are doing, in one browser tab, without those agents knowing about each other or about HTML. One screen is one instance under one mount: a second screen is a second instance under a second name, and the page is at /<mount>/ on the colony's listener.
description.not_in_scope: Not a window manager -- nothing is resized and the canvas has no camera; since 2.3.0 the dock and the OS mark are the only layers above it, and they are the screen's own furniture rather than anything an application puts there. A judgement of relevance rather than of layout: one canvas and an order -- the `ord` a view declared, then its first appearance, ties broken on identity, and never the moment a view was last written. It never invents content and never edits it -- an application brings its own components and its own tree, and this scope only wraps, places and removes them. Since 2.2.0 the compose cell is not the model: it is deterministic and offline, the `judge` beside it is the one cell that asks a provider, and the screen stands complete without it. No authentication and no TLS (R-W8-2): since 2.0.0 the display binds nothing at all, and whatever stands in front of the colony's one listener is the whole access story. No interior address either -- `params.ports` is empty, so a caller names the hive and a lane (in_view, in_withdraw and in_notice in, event and receipt out). Since 2.4.0 it is still not a window manager: the levels are a rendering of the one state, not a stack -- nothing is restored when a modal goes, and nothing on the screen remembers a gesture.
examples: an assistant sends in_view {view_id: 'today', kind: 'prose', content: {title: 'Today', body: '...'}, ttl_ms: 3600000} -- a card appears, and stops being drawn an hour later

an application sends in_view {view_id: 'colony-view', kind: 'component', components: [{name: 'colony-view-node', ...}], content: {component: 'colony-view-node', props: {...}, key: 'n.os~builder', keep: ['hand','pinned']}} -- it brings its own vocabulary and its own tree
a person clicks something on that tree -- the event leaves the hive carrying the owner and view_id it belongs to, and the member routes it back to the one agent that put the view up

an application sends in_view {view_id: 'ambient', ord: -10, kind: 'component', ...} with a child keyed `tile` on each window -- a clock, a weather tile and a countdown stand as tiles in the dock, the one that is large stands on the canvas as well, and rewriting them every twenty seconds moves nothing on the page

a person holds the OS mark on the screen and speaks -- the frames reach the `voice` cell over the socket the page already holds, the turn goes to the conversation, and the answer is played back through the mark
